-93.78400,41.60240.name: Mid-Iowa Fertility, PC
-93.78400,41.60240.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Donald C. Young, DO. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-81.97484,33.47097.name: VA Augusta Health Care System
-81.97484,33.47097.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Department of Veterans Affairs. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-74.07210,4.71100.name: ICA — Instituto Colombiano Agropecuario
-74.07210,4.71100.desc: Colombia’s agricultural regulator, approving engineered cotton and maize. Colombia is also a centre of diversity for several crops, which puts approval decisions and centre-of-origin concerns in the hands of the same body — an arrangement Mexico has fought publicly over and Colombia has not.

-74.07210,4.71100.name: Agro-Bio
-74.07210,4.71100.state: Bogotá — Asociación de Biotecnología Vegetal Agrícola
-74.07210,4.71100.desc: The industry association covering Colombia and the wider Andean region, publishing approvals, adoption figures and the case for engineered crops in Spanish for an audience the English-language trade bodies do not reach. Its reporting is where a Paraguayan or Bolivian approval is often first described for a general reader. It belongs on this map as part of the industry rather than as a source about it: an association exists to make its members' case, and it does so competently, which is precisely why its figures circulate further than the regulators' own.

-3.70380,40.41680.name: Ministerio de Agricultura (Spain) — GM cultivation register
-3.70380,40.41680.desc: Spain grows nearly all of the European Union’s engineered maize — one country accounting for almost the entire cultivated area of a bloc usually described as GM-free. The register of planted area by province is public, and it is the only place the EU’s actual cultivation footprint can be seen.

-3.70380,40.41680.name: Spanish Fertility Society — national registry
-3.70380,40.41680.desc: Spain’s fertility registry, in the country that performs more IVF cycles than any other in Europe and receives large numbers of patients from countries where treatments are restricted. The registry counts cycles; it does not count why the patients came.

-3.70380,40.41680.name: Comunidad de Madrid — animal facility licensing
-3.70380,40.41680.desc: The regional authority that issues licences to animal testing facilities in the Madrid region and inspects them. It ordered an inspection within a day of the 2021 footage being published, confirmed signs of mistreatment, and announced a suspension — then, according to the organisations pursuing the case, did not respond to requests for information about the animals still held at the site, and later allowed testing to resume. It appears on this map because sub-national regulators almost never do, and because the licensing power over a laboratory sits at that level in Spain rather than nationally. Whoever grants the licence is who a complaint has to reach, and in this instance that was a regional environment department rather than a research or health ministry.

-86.00860,39.97840.name: Beck's Hybrids
-86.00860,39.97840.desc: The largest family-owned seed company in the United States, selling maize and soy against the majors. It licenses the traits it sells rather than owning them, which is the ordinary position for an independent: the seed genetics are its own, the trait inside them belongs to somebody else, and the licence terms determine what it can offer. Independents like this are the measure of how much of the market the four majors do not directly hold.

-122.14400,37.46800.name: Impossible Foods — soy leghemoglobin
-122.14400,37.46800.desc: The heme protein that makes its burger taste of meat is produced by engineered yeast, and it is the ingredient the company had to defend. The FDA cleared it after the company sought a second review it was not required to seek, and it remains unapproved for retail sale in the EU. A plant-based product marketed to people avoiding industrial agriculture depends on a genetically engineered organism, which the company states openly and much of its market did not expect.

7.75000,48.53330.name: Boehringer Ingelheim Animal Health
7.75000,48.53330.state: Lyon and Saint-Priest, France — Boehringer Ingelheim Animal Health
7.75000,48.53330.desc: The other half of the vectored poultry market: a turkey herpesvirus construct carrying infectious bursal disease antigen, extended to a three-way version adding laryngotracheitis, and a separate fowlpox-vectored line for Newcastle disease and for H5 and H7 avian influenza. Fowlpox-vectored influenza vaccines date to the 1980s, which makes this one of the oldest deliberate uses of a recombinant organism in agriculture anywhere — older than any engineered crop on this map, and almost never counted alongside them. Over a dozen herpesvirus-vectored poultry vaccines are now commercially available across these three companies.

44.82710,41.71510.name: Ministry of Health of Georgia — assisted reproduction
44.82710,41.71510.desc: Georgia became a leading destination for cross-border surrogacy after the war in Ukraine, being one of few countries whose law recognised the intended parents from birth and at a fraction of United States costs. In June 2023 the prime minister announced that surrogacy and IVF for non-citizens would be prohibited from 1 January 2024, that Georgian women would not be permitted to be paid beyond pregnancy and birth costs, and that advertising would be banned; the health ministry was to draft the bill. Reporting through 2025 and into 2026 indicates the legislation had not been adopted and programmes for foreigners were continuing. That gap is the entry. An announced prohibition changes behaviour immediately — women interviewed at the time were rushing to begin arrangements before the announced date — whether or not it ever becomes law, and this map should record the announcement and the statute separately.

44.82710,41.71510.name: New Life Global Network
44.82710,41.71510.state: Tbilisi — with branches in several countries
44.82710,41.71510.desc: Founded in Tbilisi in 2008 by a doctor who had children through surrogacy herself, and now operating branches in Georgia, Ukraine, Mexico, South Africa, Israel, Kenya and Poland, with intended parents drawn largely from Sweden, the United Kingdom, the United States, Poland, Spain, Australia, Norway, Portugal, Japan, China and Israel. Its Georgian arm describes surrogates of several nationalities on its books. Two features are worth recording: surrogacy has been regulated in Georgia since 1997, which is why the clinics clustered there rather than anywhere nearby; and a network holding surrogates in one country, intended parents in another and a clinic in a third is a structure no single national regulator can see whole.
